classification.difficultyReason: Interpret a mass comparison as division, apply index laws and round the resulting count.

content.prompt: The mass of a hydrogen atom is approximately $1.674\times10^{-27}$ kg and the mass of an electron is approximately $9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg. How many electrons, correct to the nearest whole number, will have the same mass as a single hydrogen atom?

answer.worked:
Divide the mass of the hydrogen atom by the mass of one electron.

$$\begin{align*}N&=\frac{1.674\times10^{-27}}{9.1\times10^{-31}}\\N&=\frac{1.674}{9.1}\times10^{-27-(-31)}\\N&=\frac{837}{4550}\times10^4\\N&=\frac{167400}{91}\\N&\approx1840\end{align*}$$

Approximately $1840$ electrons have the same mass as one hydrogen atom, correct to the nearest whole number.
